title: Legacy chat transport turn-down: operational choreography, client continuity, and contract gates
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Summary: This PRD defines the operational choreography to turn down the legacy chat transport (multiplexed long-poll/SSE channel used by older SDKs) while guaranteeing client continuity through a compatibility corridor and contractual gates. Goal: remove server-side maintenance burden and reduce edge-attached state while keeping downstream apps available and providing clear, timeboxed migration obligations for customers and partners. Scope: server decommission of legacy transport endpoints, deployment of a compatibility adapter layer (short-lived), client migration playbooks, telemetry and quality gates, and legal/contract communication timeline. Out of scope: model alias changes, SDK refactors beyond lightweight adapters, and private-onprem airgap automation (handled by Private team).
prd_summary: Background: legacy chat transport carries ~12% of total chat traffic (heavy tail of enterprise integrations). It complicates autoscaling and KV cache semantics. The plan phases an adapter-based compatibility corridor (adapter will translate legacy multiplexed frames into unified inference requests) that runs for a bounded grace window. We will require client-side opt-in to the adapter via feature flags during the corridor, then issue a firm turn-down date with automated blocking for requests that do not migrate.
acceptance_criteria:
1) No client-facing increase >1% error-rate (4xx/5xx) attributable to turn-down after adapter rollout as measured by request attribution tags.
2) End-to-end 95th percentile latency for migrated flows remains within existing SLO +/- 30ms.
3) Adapter observes and logs successful translation for >=98% of legacy frames in production shadowing for 7 days before soft-fail.
4) Migration CLI and SDK adapter docs published; >=3 major client integrators confirm readiness in writing before the hard turn-down.
5) Telemetry gates (quality/regression & token-economy) green for full week during canary.
6) Legal communications sent to enterprise customers with contractual migration milestone and compensation path at least 60 days prior.
7) Rollback procedure validated in staging and documented runbook executed in a dry-run within cycle window.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Discovery, 3 weeks): traffic map, critical customer list, test harness. Phase 1 (Adapter alpha, 2 weeks): infra deploy of adapter behind feature flag; shadow translation for 14 days. Phase 2 (Canary, 1 week): route 1% live traffic to adapter; run telemetry gates. Phase 3 (Gradual ramp, 2 weeks): 1% -> 25% -> 75% with gating at each stop; reach parity. Phase 4 (Soft-deprecation, 60 days): clients receive migration deadlines, SDK tooling, guided assist. Phase 5 (Hard turn-down): block legacy transport, enable explicit error codes and developer-friendly migration hints. Each phase requires sign-off from PM, Eng on-call, Security, and Customer Success.
telemetry_gates: Metrics to monitor: legacy_transport_requests_total, adapter_translation_success_ratio, request_error_rate_by_transport, p95_latency_by_route, token_cost_delta_per-request, client-migration-progress (per-customer). Gate rules: if adapter_translation_success_ratio < 98% or request_error_rate_by-transport increases >1% absolute, pause rollout and trigger incident runbook. Token-cost regressions >5% require signoff from Optimize team.
rollback_criteria: Rollback to previous state if any of the following during canary/gradual ramp: 1) Spike in 5xxs attributable to adapter or routing change >1% absolute; 2) Latency regressions p95 exceed +100ms vs baseline; 3) Repeated client complaints from top-20 revenue accounts (>=3 distinct reports) indicating functional regression. Rollback action: disable adapter routing, re-enable legacy transport routing rules, open postmortem and extend soft-deprecation window by minimum 30 days.
migration_cli_steps: 1) Run 'ri-migrate scan --project <id>' to surface legacy usage. 2) Use 'ri-migrate generate-adapter-config --project <id>' to produce per-customer adapter mapping. 3) Validate with 'ri-migrate validate --sample-customer <id>' against staging adapter. 4) Execute 'ri-migrate cutover --project <id> --window <UTC window>' during scheduled maintenance. CLI will emit checklist and backout token. Documentation: https://confluence.redwood.ai/endpoint-harmonic/migration-cli
communication_plan: Week -8: Internal announcement and CS/SE enablement docs. Week -6: Broad customer advisory with timeline + self-serve migration kit. Week -4: Targeted outreach to top-50 integrators with migration office hours. Week -2: Reminder, SDK patches, and CLI readiness checklist. Week 0: Turn-down enforcement and public changelog. All communications follow legal-approved template; CS to track acceptance.
notes: Trade-offs discussed with Eng: building adapter reduces immediate client pressure but increases short-term infra. We expect cost delta ~+8% during adapter window, paid from runway budget. Alternative of longer compatibility corridor rejected due to autoscaling complexity and KV cache semantics. Security signoff required for adapter's frame-parsing logic; scoped fuzz tests added. Legal requested explicit SLA addendum for accounts refusing migration.
